column3: Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “them.”
“Let no man’s heart fall on him” is rendered “fail on account of him.”
“A man of war” is rendered “a warrior,” and NASB adds “but.”
“The lion and the bear” is rendered “a lion or a bear,” and “a sheep” as “a lamb.”
“From the hand of the lion” is rendered “from the paw of the lion”; “the LORD will be with you” becomes the wish “may the LORD be with you.”
The Hebrew “over his garments” is rendered “over his armor,” and “he fell short to walk” as “tried to walk.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “but.”
“There is a God belonging to Israel” is rendered “a God in Israel.”
Close to the Hebrew; “saves” is rendered “deliver.”
Close to the Hebrew; “hurried and ran” is rendered “ran quickly.”
“Was strong more than” is rendered “prevailed over.”
“Until you come to Gath” follows a reading often taken as “valley” (Hebrew גַיְא); NASB renders “as far as the valley.” “They fell” is rendered “lay.”
“If I knew” (an oath formula) is rendered “I do not know.”
